name: Machine code
subtitle: Bits become instructions
description: Start at representation, decode real RV32I words, and observe what a processor actually changes. No prior programming is assumed.

lessons.title: Bits, bytes, and a machine state
lessons.summary: Learn what a bit means before asking the processor to do anything.

lessons.title: Decode an instruction field by field
lessons.summary: Derive an ADDI encoding instead of treating hexadecimal as magic.

lessons.title: Words, byte order, and addresses
lessons.summary: Separate the way a word is displayed from the order its bytes occupy memory.

lessons.title: The arithmetic logic unit
lessons.summary: Inspect what arithmetic changes and what remains untouched.

lessons.title: Load, store, and a memory bus
lessons.summary: Move a value through RAM and learn why addresses need bounds.

lessons.title: Control flow is a change of address
lessons.summary: Decode a loop and make its stopping condition explicit.

name: Assembly
subtitle: Name the instructions
description: Write RV32I mnemonics, inspect their real encoded words, and connect branches, memory, and calls to the machine-code track.

lessons.title: Symbols, registers, and the assembler
lessons.summary: Use names to express the same state transitions you already decoded.
lessons.starter_code:
li t0,21
add t1,t0,t0
mv a0,t1
li a7,1
ecall
li a7,10
ecall

lessons.title: Signed values and bit masks
lessons.summary: Choose the interpretation an operation needs.
lessons.starter_code:
li t0,3
ori t1,t0,4
andi t1,t1,-3
mv a0,t1
li a7,1
ecall
li a7,10
ecall

lessons.title: Branches, labels, and loop invariants
lessons.summary: Explain why a loop works rather than merely observing that it stops.
lessons.starter_code:
li t0,1
li t1,6
li t2,0
loop:
add t2,t2,t0
addi t0,t0,1
blt t0,t1,loop
mv a0,t2
li a7,1
ecall
li a7,10
ecall

lessons.title: Arrays and load/store addressing
lessons.summary: Derive an element address from a base, an index, and an element size.
lessons.starter_code:
.data
numbers: .word 4,8,12,16
.text
la t0,numbers
li t1,4
li t2,0
loop:
lw t3,0(t0)
add t2,t2,t3
addi t0,t0,4
addi t1,t1,-1
bne t1,zero,loop
mv a0,t2
li a7,1
ecall
li a7,10
ecall

lessons.title: Calls, returns, and the stack
lessons.summary: Make a function call visible as a jump plus a return-address agreement.
lessons.starter_code:
li a0,21
call double_value
li a7,1
ecall
li a7,10
ecall
double_value:
addi sp,sp,-16
sw ra,12(sp)
call helper
lw ra,12(sp)
addi sp,sp,16
ret
helper:
add a0,a0,a0
ret

lessons.title: Memory-mapped device registers
lessons.summary: Treat device configuration as a documented interface, not a magic address.
lessons.starter_code:
lui t0,15
li t1,512
sw t1,0(t0)
li t1,1
sw t1,4(t0)
lw a0,4(t0)
li a7,1
ecall
li a7,10
ecall

name: C
subtitle: Control storage and layout
description: Move from instructions to functions, pointers, arrays, structures, and explicit device interfaces. Learn C with a documented bounded ILP32 interpreter.

lessons.title: From source text to an execution model
lessons.summary: Understand the C entry point, declarations, and the limits of the embedded runner.

lessons.title: Integer widths, conversion, and flags
lessons.summary: Make overflow and bit operations explicit instead of relying on accidental results.

lessons.title: Branches, loops, and a correctness argument
lessons.summary: Use a condition, an invariant, and a bound to explain an algorithm.

lessons.title: Arrays, sizes, and boundary errors
lessons.summary: Translate an index into a storage location and test the bounds deliberately.

lessons.title: Pointers and indirection
lessons.summary: Distinguish an object, a reference to it, and the value reached through that reference.

lessons.title: Functions, parameters, and local frames
lessons.summary: Connect a C call to the control-flow and storage protocol beneath it.

lessons.title: Structures and explicit data contracts
lessons.summary: Group related fields while keeping representation assumptions visible.

lessons.title: Volatile, MMIO, and configuration order
lessons.summary: Connect a language-level interface to a documented virtual device.

name: Rust
subtitle: Make ownership explicit
description: A focused systems-language bridge: integer computation, immutability, arrays, functions, and exclusive mutable access. The embedded runner is a teaching subset, not rustc.

lessons.title: Bindings, mutability, and integer intent
lessons.summary: Make permission to change a value part of its declaration.

lessons.title: Expressions, functions, and ranges
lessons.summary: Express a bounded calculation while keeping the visited values clear.

lessons.title: Borrowing and exclusive write access
lessons.summary: See why aliases need an access policy, not just an address.

lessons.title: Arrays and bounded buffers
lessons.summary: Use a compact systems-language exercise to reason about data boundaries.

name: Verilog
subtitle: Describe the logic itself
description: Learn a focused hardware-description language through gates, adders, multiplexers, and exhaustive combinational tests. Simulation is distinct from synthesis or programming an FPGA.

lessons.title: Signals, gates, and continuous assignment
lessons.summary: Describe a circuit rather than a sequential software procedure.

lessons.title: Build a half adder
lessons.summary: Derive one arithmetic circuit from a sum bit and a carry bit.

lessons.title: Multiplexers and a datapath decision
lessons.summary: Select one source without pretending the unselected input disappears.

lessons.title: Buses, comparators, and width discipline
lessons.summary: Treat a signal width as a precise part of the circuit contract.

name: Operating systems
subtitle: From reset to your own code
description: Build and host a real 512-byte x86 BIOS boot image in your workspace, inspect execution, and progress toward the included freestanding C kernel. No lesson locks.

lessons.title: Reset, firmware, and the first sector
lessons.summary: Establish who loads the first code before an operating system exists.
lessons.starter_code:
bits 16
org 0x7c00
mov ah,0x0e
mov al,66
int 0x10
hlt

lessons.title: Strings, pointers, and a boot screen
lessons.summary: Walk a zero-terminated byte sequence before a C runtime exists.
lessons.starter_code:
bits 16
org 0x7c00
start:
    xor ax, ax
    mov ds, ax
    mov si, message
    mov ah, 0x0e
print:
    lodsb
    cmp al, 0
    je done
    int 0x10
    jmp print
done:
    hlt
message:
    db "BARE METAL OS", 13, 10, "Booted from your own 512-byte image.", 13, 10, 0
lessons.example_output:
BARE METAL OS
Booted from your own 512-byte image.

lessons.title: A stack and a reusable boot routine
lessons.summary: Replace duplicated output code with a call that preserves its return path.
lessons.starter_code:
bits 16
org 0x7c00
xor ax,ax
mov ds,ax
mov si,message
call print_string
hlt
print_string:
mov ah,0x0e
again:
lodsb
cmp al,0
je finished
int 0x10
jmp again
finished:
ret
message:
db "CALL/RETURN OK",0

lessons.title: A counter, an output device, and a bounded run
lessons.summary: Use processor state to generate visible behaviour instead of replaying a picture.
lessons.starter_code:
bits 16
org 0x7c00
mov cx,10
mov ah,0x0e
mov al,48
again:
int 0x10
inc ax
loop again
hlt

lessons.title: From a boot sector to a freestanding kernel
lessons.summary: Know which responsibilities remain after the first successful screen.
lessons.starter_code:
bits 16
org 0x7c00
mov ah,0x0e
mov si,message
again:
lodsb
cmp al,0
je done
int 0x10
jmp again
done:
hlt
message:
db "Stage zero ready. Next: freestanding kernel.",0
lessons.example_output: Stage zero ready. Next: freestanding kernel.
